title: Rural living; childhood activities
description: Dale Anderson introduces the interview, taped June 19, 1975 at St. Mary's, Idaho. Anna Brebner praises rural life for raising food and good neighbors, then recalls horseback riding, skating and swimming with her siblings, especially in Coeur d'Alene.

title: Sisters' schooling; business college
description: Brebner explains that college attendance was a matter of choice in her family: one sister wanted nursing, another studied music at the University of Idaho before dying young. She describes her own year and a half of self-paced study at a Spokane business college, one of only two in the city at the time.

title: Courtship; Miltown; walking railroad tracks
description: Brebner recounts her courtship with Jim, which began in high school in 1912 while her family lived at the Miltown mill settlement about a mile out of town. She recalls walking the railroad tracks rather than the road, Jim's graduation from Palmer's school, and her own 1914 graduation in St. Mary's.

title: World War I; marriage
description: She tells of Jim's service in World War I, their limited correspondence because he was a poor letter writer, and their marriage in 1920 after his return. The couple moved to Montana, where she stopped working.

title: Marriage expectations; childbirth; doctors
description: Brebner describes wanting a big family and having seven children, all born in the St. Mary's hospital. Dr. Cornwallet served as the family doctor from 1911 until his death, with Dr. Robbins filling in on one occasion.

title: Raising children; grandchildren
description: She explains she raised her children naturally with little formal guidance, never pushing them in schoolwork. She reports on her seventeen grandchildren, four great-grandchildren, one grandson who left the University of Idaho for lack of money, and five grandchild weddings in a single year.

title: Lifestyle; travel; vacations
description: Brebner says her lifestyle has changed little and that travel has mostly meant visiting relatives. She recalls regular trips to North Bend, visits to Jim's widowed sister in Oakland, and travel by bus, plane, car and train.

title: Trains; steamboats; fairs
description: She fondly recalls passenger trains through St. Mary's and arriving by the Coeur d'Alene river steamboat, remembering boats named the Georgie Oaks, Idaho and Flyer. She also compares the Spokane and Seattle world's fairs, strongly preferring Spokane's, and looks at a book of riverboat photographs with Jim.

title: Daily housework; correspondence; friends
description: Brebner describes her morning routine of cooking, baking bread twice weekly and making cookies, replacing letters with cassette recordings as her typing and eyesight decline. She names old friends still in town, including Margie Smith who runs the credit bureau and Mrs. Scribner.

title: Town growth; new industries
description: Brebner discusses how the plywood mill and railroad have brought many new people to St. Mary's, making longtime residents feel like strangers in church but reducing unemployment. She describes the town as exceptionally friendly, notes her children do not want to leave, and says her oldest daughter's family hopes to return after retirement.
